comments.text: Lines 5-7: ON ERROR RUN, so that any error starts the logo again, and `*FX200,2`, which makes BREAK clear memory (the MOS's &0258 = 2).

Lines 10-40: VDU 6 (output on), then VDU 23 defines characters 224-246, eight rows of eight pixels each. 224-234 are the slope, the blocks and the upright of a small figure 4; 235-239 hold the upper rows of the letters MAT beside the foot of the upright, and 240-246 their last rows. The MOS keeps them at &0C00 onwards, where the menu's hand-over still holds them.

Line 50: MODE 1, cursor off, the graphics origin moved 128 units right (VDU 29), logical colour 0 made white (VDU 19,0,7) and the screen cleared in colour 3, white in Mode 1's palette, so the whole screen is white. Colours 1 and 2 become blue and cyan; `Another adventure from....` is written at the graphics cursor in blue (VDU 5). Then thirteen points from line 160, each a MOVE or a filled triangle (PLOT 85), paint the outline of a large 4 in colour 0: white on white, so far invisible.

Lines 60-80: char$ is built from the 96 codes of lines 120-130: characters 224-246 with line feeds (10) and backspaces (8) between them, so that one PRINT draws the small 4 with MAT at its foot, eight rows tall. It is printed up column 28 (PROCv: rows 21, 19 and so on to 1), then seven times on a diagonal from column 28, row 1 to column 16, row 9, two columns left and one or two rows down a step, then at rows 14 and 12 of column 16 (PROCv), then nine times along row 15 from column 16 to 32, each copy in blue and cyan by turns (COLOUR 1 and 2), so the copies build the strokes of the large 4.

Line 90: `EDUCATIONAL` and `SOFTWARE` in blue under the 4, its outline DRAWn in blue round the triangles, and last VDU 19,3,6, which turns colour 3, the background, from white to cyan. The white triangles of line 50 appear at that moment as the large 4 behind the small ones (live: the screen stays white until this line).
Line 100: a delay loop of 5000 empty steps, then CHAIN the menu, UNEM.

Lines 120-130, DATA: the 96 character codes of char$, read by line 60. Each row of the small 4 ends with a line feed and the backspaces that take the cursor to the next row's first column, one column further left while the slope widens and the same column after it: rows of 3, 4, 5, 6 and 7 characters for the slope, 7 for the bar, then two rows of seven for the letters MAT and the foot of the upright.
PROCv(a,b,d), lines 140-150: prints char$ at column d+4 on rows a, a-2 and so on up to b, blue and cyan by turns; a vertical stroke of the large 4.

Line 160, DATA: thirteen triples x, y, z for line 50, in graphics units from the moved origin. z=1 moves there, z=2 fills a triangle with the two points before; the thirteen make the large 4's upright, its diagonal and its bar.

Six bytes of &E5 after the program's end mark, inside the file's catalogue length of 1,869: &E5 is the byte a newly formatted DFS disc holds, so the length was given six bytes more than the program. BASIC never reads them.
